retry.fallbackChains warns 'references unknown model' for config-declared providers when the discovery cache is cold (e.g. after an update bumps the cache namespace)

## Description

When the SQLite model-discovery cache has no row for a config-declared provider, `retry.fallbackChains` validation runs before background discovery has populated the registry, so models that exist and work are reported as unknown:

```
Warning: retry.fallbackChains key references unknown model: litellm/Qwen3.8-27B
Warning: Fallback chain for model 'litellm/Qwen3.8-27B' references unknown model: litellm/Qwen3.8-27B-hetzner
Warning: Fallback chain for role 'advisor' references unknown model: litellm/gpt-5.6-luna
```

Discovery finishes ~1 s later and the models are all present, but the warnings are pushed into `configWarnings` once and never retracted, so in the TUI they stay in the header for the whole session.

The practical trigger is `omp update`: the LiteLLM discovery cache is namespaced `litellm:rich-vN:<hash(baseUrl)>` and a release that bumps `rich-vN` orphans every existing row, so the first launch on the new build starts cold. My `models.db` holds the ladder `rich-v5`, `rich-v6`, `rich-v7`, `rich-v8` accumulated over three weeks, and the warning timestamps line up with the first launch under a new namespace: warnings at `09:35:18.388`, the `rich-v8` row written at `09:35:19`.

This is the same *symptom* as #1052 (ollama-cloud, fixed by #1082) and #9205 (credential-keyed cache ids, fixed by #9210 via `hydrateCredentialScopedModelCaches`), but a different cause: those fixes make specific cache rows *findable*, whereas here there is genuinely no row yet and the validator has no "discovery pending" state. #9210's hydration pass is awaited at `sdk.ts:1343` but covers only opencode-zen/-go/copilot, so providers declared in `models.yml` remain exposed.

## Steps to Reproduce

Any provider declared in `models.yml` whose catalog comes from discovery will do; this uses LiteLLM.

1. Declare the provider in `~/.omp/agent/models.yml`:

```yaml
providers:
  litellm:
    baseUrl: https://litellm.example.net/v1
    apiKey: sk-...
    api: openai-completions
```

2. Reference discovered models in `~/.omp/agent/config.yml`:

```yaml
retry:
  fallbackChains:
    litellm/Qwen3.8-27B:
      - litellm/Qwen3.8-27B-hetzner
    advisor:
      - litellm/gpt-5.6-luna
modelRoles:
  advisor: openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol:max
```

3. Let a normal run populate the cache, then simulate the post-update cold namespace:

```bash
sqlite3 ~/.omp/agent/models.db \
  "delete from model_cache where provider_id like 'litellm:rich-v8%';"
```

4. Start `omp`. The three warnings render in the header; `~/.omp/logs/omp.<date>.<pid>.log` records them a fraction of a second before the `rich-v8` row is rewritten with all of the supposedly unknown models in it.

Controls run alongside: a **stale** row (`updated_at` aged 48 h) produces no warnings, so the trigger is a missing row rather than TTL expiry; `omp -p '…'` with a deleted row logs the same three warnings, so this is not TUI-specific — the TUI is just where they stay visible.

## Expected Behavior

A selector that discovery is about to supply should not be reported as unknown. Either validation waits for the in-flight discovery for providers whose discovery state is pending, or the warnings are re-evaluated and cleared once discovery lands.

## Root Cause

Validation is synchronous in the `TurnRecovery` constructor, and the discovery that fills the registry for config-declared providers is fire-and-forget.

`packages/coding-agent/src/session/turn-recovery.ts:252` (constructor) → `:1305-1309`:

```ts
#validateRetryFallbackChains(): void {
    validateRetryFallbackChains(this.#host.settings, this.#host.modelRegistry, message =>
        this.#host.configWarnings.push(message),
    );
}
```

`packages/coding-agent/src/session/retry-fallback-chains.ts:189` and `:217-219` treat "absent from the registry" as "unknown" — there is no pending-discovery state:

```ts
} else if (!modelRegistry.find(parsedKey.provider, parsedKey.id)) {
    report(`retry.fallbackChains key references unknown model: ${key}`);
}
...

## Summary

In v0.6.3rc1, running the ANE Split Tuner on a model whose current engine is the **DFlash engine** fails before the first calibration step:

```
RuntimeError: Loaded engine does not expose its model
```

This is a **different failure from #2908** (ANE Tuner OOM at _VERIFY_SLOT, 48 GB machine): here there is no memory pressure — the crash happens immediately at `_calibrate_components`, the moment the tuner tries to reach into the live engine for the model object. It is **deterministic**: it fails every time the model is loaded with DFlash enabled.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Hardware | Apple **M5 Max**, **128 GB** unified memory |
| OS | macOS 26.6.2 (Build 25G83) |
| oMLX | **0.6.3rc1**, app build **2388** |
| Target model | `mlx-community/Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp4` (~17.8 GB loaded) |
| Draft model | `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` |

Reproduced twice in one hour (11:30:36 and 11:42:54), same model, same path.

## Per-model settings at crash time

```json
{
  "dflash_enabled": true,
  "qwen35_ane_prefill_enabled": true,
  "qwen35_ane_prefill_sequence_length": 2048,
  "qwen35_ane_prefill_fraction": 0.53,
  "qwen35_ane_prefill_max_layers": 64,
  "qwen35_ane_prefill_dual_ane": true,
  "qwen35_ane_prefill_gdn": true
}
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Load any model with DFlash enabled (`dflash_enabled: true` + a compatible draft checkpoint).
2. Open **Hardware Acceleration → ANE Configuration** in the web dashboard / app.

4. The tuner fails immediately, before any calibration bank is compiled. (Workaround: turn DFlash off, let the model reload through the regular LM/VLM engine, then run the tuner.)

```text
2026-08-20 11:30:36,693 - omlx.admin.ane_tuning - ERROR - [-] - ANE tuning failed for Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp4

    model = _loaded_model(engine)

The engine had been loaded as the DFlash engine right before:

```text
2026-08-20 11:31:41,307 - omlx.engine_pool - INFO - [-] - DFlash enabled for Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp4, draft=/.../z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2

`run_tuning` (ane_tuning.py:818-822) expects to stage a regular engine:

[BUG]: Chat prompt_logprobs only returned on nvext, not on the OpenAI choice

### Describe the Bug

Top-level `prompt_logprobs` on `/v1/chat/completions` is accepted (`CommonExt`) and forwarded to the vLLM worker. The worker computes the payload and stashes it on `engine_data.prompt_logprobs`. The Rust postprocessor only copies it onto `nvext.prompt_logprobs`, and only when the client also sends `nvext.extra_fields: ["prompt_logprobs"]`.

Native vLLM returns the same data at the **response root** (`prompt_logprobs`) from the top-level request field alone. A vLLM-compatible client that only sets `"prompt_logprobs": N` gets HTTP 200 with no prompt logprobs in the OpenAI-shaped body.

`choices[0].logprobs` is generation-token logprobs (`content` / `refusal`) and is a different field.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Serve a chat model with Dynamo's vLLM backend and the Rust OpenAI frontend (`python -m dynamo.frontend` / `--dyn-chat-processor dynamo`).

2. POST `/v1/chat/completions` with top-level `prompt_logprobs` and **no** `nvext`:

```bash
curl -sS http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "<served-model>",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "1 + 1 = ?"}],
    "max_tokens": 1,
    "temperature": 0,
    "prompt_logprobs": 2
  }'
```

3. Inspect the JSON:

```bash
python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); c=d["choices"][0]; print({
  "top_level_prompt_logprobs": d.get("prompt_logprobs"),
  "choice_prompt_logprobs": c.get("prompt_logprobs"),
  "choice_logprobs": c.get("logprobs"),
  "nvext_prompt_logprobs": (d.get("nvext") or {}).get("prompt_logprobs"),
})'
```

4. Repeat the same request with the nvext opt-in:

```json
{
  "model": "<served-model>",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "1 + 1 = ?"}],
  "max_tokens": 1,
  "temperature": 0,
  "prompt_logprobs": 2,
  "nvext": { "extra_fields": ["prompt_logprobs"] }
}
```

5. Send the step-2 payload to native vLLM `/v1/chat/completions` and compare the response-root `prompt_logprobs` field.

### Expected Behavior

When the request includes top-level `prompt_logprobs`, the computed array should appear on the OpenAI response **root** without requiring `nvext.extra_fields`. That matches native vLLM.

Native vLLM shape: `prompt_logprobs` is an array next to `choices` (first prompt position is often `null` because there is no preceding-token probability). Length matches `usage.prompt_tokens`. Entries are token-id maps with `logprob` (native also includes `rank` and `decoded_token`).

`nvext.prompt_logprobs` can remain as an optional extra when `extra_fields` asks for it; it should not be the only way to read the data.

### Actual Behavior

Step 2: HTTP 200, response-root `prompt_logprobs` is absent, `choices[0].prompt_logprobs` is absent, `nvext` is absent. Looks like a no-op.

Step 4: `nvext.prompt_logprobs` is populated. That shows the engine already computed the values; the frontend is gating them behind nvext.

### Environment

- Dynamo frontend: Rust `/v1/chat/completions`
- Backend: dynamo-vLLM (worker serializes `RequestOutput.prompt_logprobs` onto `engine_data`)
- Native vLLM chat completions on the same payload returns top-level `prompt_logprobs` (confirmed on `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507`)

### Additional Context

Gating is `NvExtResponseFieldSelection::from_nvext`, which only sets `prompt_logprobs: true` when `"prompt_logprobs"` is in `nvext.extra_fields`. `chat_completions/delta.rs` then passes the engine payload into `build_response_nvext`.

The `/v1/generate` path already returns `prompt_logprobs` when requested on that API. Chat completions should emit the equivalent on the OpenAI response root.

A fix can stay in `lib/llm`:

1. When `CommonExt.prompt_logprobs` is `Some`, emit the payload even if `nvext.extra_fields` is omitted.
2. Copy it onto the OpenAI response root as `prompt_logprobs` (native vLLM). `dynamo-protocols` `CreateChatCompletionResponse` currently has no such field, so this may need a field on `NvCreateChatCompletionResponse` (or a protocols bu

Draft: z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-GGUF (Q4_K_M)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

DFlash speculative decoding (--spec-type draft-dflash) fails to load when --split-mode tensor is used with multiple CUDA devices. The same setup works correctly with --spec-type draft-mtp, and DFlash itself works when switching to --split-mode layer, so the issue appears specific to the interaction between DFlash and tensor split.

The DFlash draft model shares the target model's output.weight (per the auto-setup that reuses the target's embedding + lm_head). Under tensor split that tensor lives in the combined Meta() device spanning both GPUs, and the draft context cannot operate on it.

There is also a second, likely related failure: with tensor split and DFlash, the server crashes earlier during warmup with GGML_ASSERT(obj_new) failed at ggml.c:1804. Passing --no-warmup gets past that point and surfaces the output.weight error.

Steps to reproduce:

2. Same command plus --no-warmup -> fails when loading the draft model.

3. Same command with --split-mode layer instead of tensor -> loads and generates correctly.

4. Same command with --spec-type draft-mtp and --split-mode tensor -> loads and generates correctly (~39 t/s).

Reducing --ctx-size from 122880 to 8192 does not change either failure.

Performance comparison on this hardware, same prompt:
- MTP + tensor split, n_max=2: 39.4 t/s
- DFlash + layer split, n_max=7, greedy: 15.7 t/s, 24.5% acceptance
- DFlash + layer split, n_max=2, greedy: 23.1 t/s, 54.6% acceptance

Because DFlash cannot currently be combined with tensor split, users on multi-GPU setups have to trade away the tensor-split speedup to use it, which on this hardware makes DFlash a net loss despite reasonable draft acceptance.

## What happened?

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Load a large model (`unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` UD-Q4_K_XL + `mmproj-F16.gguf`) in Unsloth Studio[cite: 4].
2. Set configuration for full VRAM offloading (`-ngl -1`)[cite: 4].
3. Observe that system RAM spikes as the model is read into memory, but is never released back to the OS pool despite the model residing entirely in GPU VRAM.

**Expected behavior:**
When full GPU offloading is utilized (`-ngl -1`), system memory should be released after the model and KV cache are loaded into VRAM.

**Actual behavior:**
The Studio backend orchestrator launches `llama-server.exe` using default memory mapping (`mmap`) as logged in "backend-backend-1786854602953-2-s01_2.log"[cite: 4]. Because `--no-mmap` is absent from the command arguments, the Windows memory manager caches the ~17.6 GB of model and projection files in the system working set indefinitely[cite: 4]. Additionally, PyTorch and the Python runtime retain memory on the heap following the `torch warm` initialization sequence shown in "server-20260815-213003-pid19064_2.log"[cite: 5].

**Model and operation involved:**
Inference and loading of `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF` (variant UD-Q4_K_XL) and `mmproj-F16.gguf`[cite: 4].

Bug Report: kvarn6 KV-quantization causes massive performance regression on ROCm (RX 7900 XTX)

**Issue:** Using KV-quantization `kvarn6` results in extremely slow performance compared to `q8_0` on AMD ROCm hardware.

## Performance Comparison

Both tests used the **same prompt** (10,410 tokens) and identical settings except for KV quantization.

> **Note:** The kvarn6 run was canceled early due to excessive runtime.

| Metric | q8_0 | kvarn6 | Regression |
|--------|------|--------|------------|
| Prompt Processing | **821.19 tokens/sec** | **53.79 tokens/sec** | **~15.3x slower** |
| Text Generation | **29.52 tokens/sec** | **1.34 tokens/sec** | **~22x slower** |

This is a severe performance regression that makes kvarn6 practically unusable.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use llama.cpp build `11192 (ee8754c57)` with ROCm backend on Windows
2. Load a large model (tested with Qwen3.6-27B-Fable-Fusion-Q4_K_M)
3. Run with full offload (`-ngl 99`) and flash attention (`-fa 1`)
4. Compare these two configurations:

**q8_0 (baseline):**
```bash
llama-server.exe -m <model> -ngl 99 -fa 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -c 40000
```

**kvarn6 (regression):**
```bash
llama-server.exe -m <model> -ngl 99 -fa 1 -ctk kvarn6 -ctv kvarn6 -c 40000
```

## System Information

- **GPU:** AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (24 GB VRAM)
- **CPU:** AMD Ryzen 9 7900X 12-Core
- **RAM:** 64 GB
- **OS:** Windows
- **Backend:** ROCm (HIP), NO_VMM = 1
- **Build:** 11192 (ee8754c57) with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64
- **Model:** Qwen3.6-27B-Fable-Fusion (Q4_K_M, 65 layers, 27.32B params, 17.22 GiB)

## Relevant Log Excerpts

**q8_0 performance:**
```
prompt processing, n_tokens = 10410, progress = 1.00, t = 11.93 s / 872.56 tokens per second
prompt eval time = 12681.67 ms / 10414 tokens (1.22 ms per token, 821.19 tokens per second)
eval time = 73468.79 ms / 2169 tokens (33.87 ms per token, 29.52 tokens per second)
```

**kvarn6 performance (run canceled after ~5.5 minutes):**
```
prompt processing, n_tokens = 10410, progress = 1.00, t = 193.54 s / 53.79 tokens per second
n_decoded = 144, tg = 1.34 t/s
```

## Expected Behavior

`kvarn6` should provide competitive or better performance than `q8_0` while using less VRAM, or at least not be an order of magnitude slower.

## Actual Behavior

`kvarn6` is **15-22x slower** than `q8_0` on ROCm hardware, making it impractical for use.

## Additional Notes

- This appears to be ROCm-specific; the kvarn6 implementation may not be optimized for AMD GPUs
- The issue affects both prompt processing and token generation equally severely
- The kvarn6 run was manually canceled due to excessive runtime; actual degradation may be even more severe over longer generations

The failure is **not monotonic in depth** — there is a degradation zone with occasional passes — but everything ≥ ~174k observed so far fails deterministically.

The same needle test at 243k tokens **PASSES on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (30 GDN layers) on the same build, same server, same machine**, which makes this look like a depth × linear-layer-count effect in the recurrent-state path rather than a per-backend kernel bug.

[Bug]: DFlash2 draft models fail to load on main — #52560 reverted the `decoder_layer_cls` indirection added by #52816

### Your current environment

```
vLLM: 0.26.1rc1.dev1117+g30b34171b (built from main, VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1)
GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (sm_120, 48GB)

Target: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (NVFP4, compressed-tensors), --kv-cache-dtype fp8
Draft:  incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2
```

### Describe the bug

Any `DFlash2DraftModel` checkpoint fails to load on current `main`. The DFlash2 decoder layers are never constructed, so the checkpoint's convolution weights have no destination:

```
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'layers.0.attention_conv' in DFlash2Qwen3Model.
The available parameters belonging to layers.0 (DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer) are:
{'layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj.weight', 'layers.0.self_attn.k_norm.weight',
 'layers.0.self_attn.o_proj.weight', 'layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight',
 'layers.0.self_attn.q_norm.weight', 'layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight',
 'layers.0.input_layernorm.weight', 'layers.0.post_attention_layernorm.weight'}
```

Note the reported layer type: `DFlash2Qwen3Model` built `DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer` layers instead of `DFlash2Qwen3DecoderLayer`.

### Root cause

#52816 ("[Spec Decode] DFlash2: local convolution + candidate selector") introduced two parallel extension points in `qwen3_dflash.py` so the DFlash2 subclasses could override them:

- `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM.model_cls`
- `DFlashQwen3Model.decoder_layer_cls`

**#52560 ("[Model] Add Qwen3-Omni DSpark support") reverted the second one.** Per `git log -L442,443:vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py`:

```
2f55ef254 [Model] Add Qwen3-Omni DSpark support (#52560)
-                self.decoder_layer_cls(
+                DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer(

b389ac294 [Spec Decode] DFlash2: local convolution + candidate selector (#52816)
-                DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer(
+                self.decoder_layer_cls(
```

`2f55ef254` landed after `b389ac294`, and also dropped the `decoder_layer_cls` class attribute from `DFlashQwen3Model`. `model_cls` survived, which is why `DFlash2Qwen3Model` is instantiated correctly and the failure looks confusing -- only the layer class is wrong.

`qwen3_dflash2.py` still sets `decoder_layer_cls = DFlash2Qwen3DecoderLayer` (line 236), so the override is now dead code. A code search for `decoder_layer_cls` on the default branch returns exactly one file -- the consumer, with no definer.

This looks like a merge-resolution mistake rather than an intentional revert: #52560 is about Qwen3-Omni DSpark and has no reason to change how DFlash layers are constructed.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
```

### Fix

Restoring the two lines #52816 added is sufficient:

```diff
 @support_torch_compile
 class DFlashQwen3Model(nn.Module):
+    decoder_layer_cls = DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer
+
     hf_to_vllm_mapper = WeightsMapper(
@@
         self.layers = nn.ModuleList(
             [
-                DFlashQwen3DecoderLayer(
+                self.decoder_layer_cls(
                     current_vllm_config,
```

With that applied, DFlash2 loads and runs correctly. Measured on one RTX PRO 5000 (sm_120), Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 target, fp8 KV cache, `--max-model-len 262144`, single stream, 5 fixed prompts, thinking disabled:

| spec method | decode | prefill @18.7K | KV pool |
|---|---|---|---|
| MTP spec=3 | 112.5 tok/s | 6,288 tok/s | 515,501 tok |
| **DFlash2 spec=7** | **203.0 tok/s** | 6,516 tok/s | 359,511 tok |
| DSpark spec=7 | 141.4 tok/s | 6,440 tok/s | 304,558 tok |

Decode-only mean acceptance length for DFlash2 was 4.71, and output was correct on inspection -- so the regression is purely the missing extension point, not a deeper problem with the DFlash2 path.

eval bug: draft-mtp roughly halves prompt processing on multi-GPU layer split (single GPU is fine)

### Name and Version

build 10499 (6d0549831), reproduces identically on 6c8dcaa7a (Aug 3)

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

## Environment

- build 10499 (6d0549831), also reproduced on 6c8dcaa7a from Aug 3 — not recent
- Linux, CUDA 12.0 + Vulkan build
- RTX 4090 Laptop 16GB (internal) + RX 7900 XTX 24GB (RADV)


### Models

- models: unsloth Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF (Q6_K_XL / Q3_K_XL), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M —
  all with nextn_predict_layers=1
- -fa on, -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Just spent the last two days knees deep in benchmark after benchmark with a bench harness I built out as I tried to optimize my setup. Essentialy a llama-bench-replica for all the flags.

I found some anomolies with MTP. After doing my best to track them down, I'm convinced these are unnexpected behavior. tldr: MTP is still a net gain, but my pp drops from ~1k to ~500 t/s. Wins back on my workloads to pay itself off in the benefits on tg, but... I'm pretty confident that hit hints at a bigger issue. I do think tb4 is probably exacerbating the issue, but my suspicion is this is an issue for others with more standard setups as well.

To be clear, on single gpu, it's like a 3% penalty to use MTP. When I split across my two gpus, it's like a 100% penalty. something is off. and settings the `draft mtp device` flag to set it to one gpu gets me back only 8% of that loss.

## What happens

With `--spec-type draft-mtp` enabled, prompt processing drops to roughly half speed
whenever the model is split across two GPUs with `--split-mode layer`. On a single GPU
the overhead is small. Same model file, same flags, only the device assignment changes.

I went down a few wrong paths on this (thought it was my eGPU, then thought it was
CUDA-specific) so I ended up with a fairly complete matrix. 22k token cold prompt (huge code file + give me a code review of this),
prompt eval t/s from server timings:

| config | no MTP | draft-mtp | worse by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.8-27B Q3_K_XL, RTX 4090 solo (CUDA) | 766 | 742 | 3% |
| Qwen3.8-27B Q3_K_XL, 7900 XTX solo (Vulkan) | 572 | 505 | 13% |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q4_K_M, 7900 XTX solo | 1593 | 1307 | 22% |
| Qwen3.8-27B Q6_K_XL, CUDA0+Vulkan2 layer split | 973 | 532 | 83% |
| Qwen3.8-27B Q3_K_XL, CUDA0+Vulkan2 layer split | 1007 | 555 | 82% |
| Qwen3.8-27B Q6_K_XL, Vulkan1+Vulkan2 layer split | 754 | 376 | 100% |

disclosure: *"no MTP" rows use --spec-type ngram-map-k4v, which doesn't touch prefill and matches
the no-spec prefill rate--I tested locally, match was within 1% when I did both on many runs.
And for clarity: last row is the same NVIDIA card via Vulkan instead of CUDA,
so no CUDA anywhere, and it's even worse. its no-MTP figure is llama-bench pp8192 on the
same split. to be clear, llama-bench and llama-server rates agree within ~1% on the row where I have both. Row 6's no-MTP figure is llama-bench pp8192 on the same split.

The `graphs reused` counter roughly halves with MTP on in every config (e.g. 960 ->
425 on the CUDA split pair, 897 -> 346 on Vulkan solo), but that on its own doesn't
seem to cost much... the solo rows eat the same reuse loss and barely slow down. The
expensive part only shows up when the layers are split across devices.

## Why I think this happens (or I should say, why AI tells me this is possibly happening--this is above my paygrade)

> In common/speculative.cpp the MTP process() hook runs a synchronous catch-up decode in
the draft context for every prefill ubatch (unless the model is mem-shared; the
"e.g Gemma4" comment). On a layer split that means every ubatch the pipeline between
the two GPUs gets broken by a decode on another context, so the ubatch overlap
(GGML_SCHED_MAX_COPIES) never gets going. That would explain why single GPU is nearly
free but any split pays ~2x regardless of backend.

Misc. bug: ROCm FA: only q8_0/q8_0 and q4_0/q4_0 KV cache works, all other types cause 34 graph splits (pp512 drops ~68%)

### Name and Version

llama-b10639-bin-win-rocm-7.14-x64
build: 5e6a37cb1 (10639)
built with Clang 20.1.8 for Windows x86_64


### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server.exe -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0

or

llama-bench.exe -m Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf -ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

## Summary

On the ROCm backend, using any q5_0 KV cache type (either K or V) causes the compute graph to fragment from 2 splits into 34 splits. This pushes ~550-580 MiB of compute to the CPU host buffer and causes a ~68% regression in prompt processing throughput.

The issue is **specific to the ROCm backend**. The same build on Vulkan handles q5_0 KV cache correctly (2 splits, no regression). A fork of llama.cpp (build 11429) also handles it correctly on ROCm.

## Environment

- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), 24 GB VRAM
- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 7900X
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_XL (16.34 GiB, 27.32 B params)
- Flash attention: enabled (`-fa 1`)

## Benchmark results

| KV Cache | graph splits | GPU compute buf | CPU compute buf | pp512 | tg128 |
|----------|:-----------:|:--------------:|:--------------:|:-----:|:-----:|
| q8_0 / q8_0 (ROCm) | 2 | 786.53 MiB | 161.53 MiB | 957.11 t/s | 37.53 t/s |
| q8_0 / q5_0 (ROCm) | **34** | **122.28 MiB** | **551.28 MiB** | **300.10 t/s** | **27.96 t/s** |
| q5_0 / q5_0 (ROCm) | **34** | **122.28 MiB** | **580.53 MiB** | **302.49 t/s** | **28.39 t/s** |
| q8_0 / q8_0 (Vulkan, same build) | 2 | 270.53 MiB | 158.53 MiB | 771.39 t/s | 37.17 t/s |
| q8_0 / q5_0 (Vulkan, same build) | **2** | **295.03 MiB** | **183.03 MiB** | **762.60 t/s** | **37.01 t/s** |

The trigger is q5_0 in the KV cache. It does not matter whether it's used for K, V, or both. The broken GPU compute buffer size is identical (122.28 MiB) in both q8_0/q5_0 and q5_0/q5_0 cases, confirming it's the same code path.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build llama.cpp with ROCm support (or use a prebuilt ROCm binary)
2. Run `llama-bench -m <model.gguf> -ctk q5_0 -ctv q5_0` (or `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q5_0`)
3. Observe ~68% pp512 regression vs. q8_0/q8_0
4. Compare with the same build on Vulkan — no regression

## Expected behavior

q5_0 KV cache should perform similarly to q8_0 KV cache (within a small margin) when using flash attention, as it does on Vulkan and on the beellama fork (build 11429).

## Key log evidence

The main model's `sched_reserve` output:

**Working (q8_0/q8_0, ROCm):**

sched_reserve: ROCm0 compute buffer size = 786.53 MiB
sched_reserve: ROCm_Host compute buffer size = 161.53 MiB
sched_reserve: graph nodes = 4135
sched_reserve: graph splits = 2

**Broken (q5_0/q5_0, ROCm):**

sched_reserve: ROCm0 compute buffer size = 122.28 MiB
sched_reserve: ROCm_Host compute buffer size = 580.53 MiB
sched_reserve: graph nodes = 4135
sched_reserve: graph splits = 34

**Working (q8_0/q5_0, Vulkan, same build 10639):**

sched_reserve: Vulkan1 compute buffer size = 295.03 MiB
sched_reserve: Vulkan_Host compute buffer size = 183.03 MiB
sched_reserve: graph nodes = 4135
sched_reserve: graph splits = 2


The 4135-node graph is the main model forward pass. The 34 splits mean 32 extra GPU↔CPU synchronization points per step.

Not yet identified. The issue is present in build 10639.

ANE prefill is silently bypassed when DFlash is enabled — tuner recommends a config serving then ignores (0.6.3rc2, M3 Ultra)

**Summary.** The new ANE/CPU prefill path works, and delivers roughly the advertised gain
(**+31% prefill** here). But when `dflash_enabled` is true, the ANE path is **silently
skipped**: the `qwen35_ane_prefill_*` settings are accepted, no warning is logged, zero
ANE lines appear in the log, and prefill throughput is identical to ANE-off. Meanwhile the
ANE tuner — which per the rc2 notes "stages candidates without DFlash wrappers" — happily
measures the gain and recommends enabling ANE, a recommendation the DFlash serving path
then never uses. Users who run DFlash (most, presumably, since it's the headline feature)
will believe ANE is on when it does nothing.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Hardware | Mac Studio, Apple M3 Ultra, 256 GB unified memory |
| macOS | 26.5.2 |
| oMLX | 0.6.3rc2 (`oMLX-0.6.3rc2-macos26-27.dmg`) |

| Target model | `Jundot/Qwen3.8-27B-oQ4e-fp16-mtp` |
| Draft model | `incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, `dflash_block_size: 5` |
| Other | `enable_thinking: false`; tuner-recommended ANE values applied in full (below) |

Tuner recommendation (from `/admin/api/bench/ane-tune`, 90 configs, completed):

```json
{"enabled": true, "mlp_fraction": 0.45, "gdn_enabled": true, "gdn_fraction": 0.4,

## Measurements — full 2×2

**Where are you using Unsloth?**

- PyTorch: `2.10.0`
- Transformers: `5.5.0`
- MLX: `0.32.1`
- psutil: `7.2.2`

## What happened?

A recently introduced Metal context-memory guard refuses to load a Qwen3.8-27B Unsloth Dynamic GGUF configuration that previously worked reliably and still works when the provided overcommit override is enabled.

The Run Settings panel estimates that this configuration needs **38.06 GiB** of unified memory and displays:

```text
This fits the machine, but not what is free right now. If that memory is not the model being replaced, the context will be fitted down or the load refused.
```

At the time, macOS Activity Monitor showed approximately 30 GB of unified memory in use and approximately 32 GB remaining/available.

Before this refusal behavior was introduced, I repeatedly ran this same model at the same manually selected 131,072-token context without kernel panics or other stability problems. When it is running I often have 8GB free of unified memory.

Unsloth Desktop now returns HTTP 500 and refuses to start llama-server. The error recommends setting:

```text
UNSLOTH_ALLOW_METAL_CTX_OVERCOMMIT=1
```

There is no way to enable this through the desktop UI. Adding an `export` to `.zshrc` also does not affect Unsloth when it is launched normally from Finder or the Dock.

The workaround requires launching Unsloth specially from Terminal, using `launchctl`, or creating a custom macOS LaunchAgent. This should be a supported option in the desktop application's settings.

I subsequently launched Unsloth with `UNSLOTH_ALLOW_METAL_CTX_OVERCOMMIT=1`. Without changing the model or Run Settings, the model loaded successfully and generated responses. This demonstrates that the hard preflight refusal can reject a configuration that actually runs on this machine.

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Launch Unsloth Desktop normally from Finder or the Dock on an M1 Ultra Mac with 64 GB unified memory.
2. Select model repository `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF`.
3. Select `Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q6_K_XL.gguf`.
4. Set Context Length manually to `131072`.
5. Leave KV Cache Dtype at `f16`.
6. Leave Speculative Decoding, Parallel Slots, Batch Size and Micro-batch Size on Auto.
7. Keep Tensor Parallelism off and Vision on.
8. Leave GPU Memory at Default and Mmap/Mlock, Checkpoints and Cache RAM on Auto.
9. Add these Extra Arguments:

```text
--rope-scaling yarn --yarn-orig-ctx 32768
```

10. Attempt to load the model.
11. Observe the HTTP 500 Metal unified-memory refusal.
12. Quit Unsloth completely.
13. Relaunch the desktop application with `UNSLOTH_ALLOW_METAL_CTX_OVERCOMMIT=1` in its process environment.
14. Load the exact same model configuration.
15. Observe that llama-server loads the model and successfully generates responses.

**Expected behavior:**

The existing safe behavior can remain the default, but Unsloth Desktop should provide a supported, persistent UI option that allows an informed user to override the estimated Metal memory limit.

**Environment**
- Hardware: MacBook/Mac with Apple M4 Max
- oMLX version: 0.6.3
- Model: `Qwen3.8-27B-oQ4e-mtp` (VLM, single image input)
- Trigger: occurred while running a long task / long-running server session

**Description**

During a long-running session, a chat request failed at prefill with a Metal command buffer error. The request had a large prompt (85,917 tokens) with strong prefix-cache reuse — 81,920 of those tokens (20 blocks) were served from the paged SSD cache and reconstructed successfully across 64 layers. Prefill then failed immediately afterward with:

```
ANE input pack command buffer failed; canceling this dispatch:
Error Domain=MTLCommandBufferErrorDomain Code=4
"Ignored (for causing prior/excessive GPU errors)"
(00000004:kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorSubmissionsIgnored)
```

This bubbled up as a chat-streaming error (`Error during chat streaming`) and the request was aborted.

**Key detail:** The wording "Ignored (for causing prior/excessive GPU errors)" indicates the ANE/GPU driver had already accumulated prior command-buffer failures *before* this request, and started refusing new submissions — this specific request looks like it was just the one that surfaced the already-degraded GPU/ANE state, not necessarily the root cause itself. Misc. bug: GBNF parser rejects escaped hyphen (`\-`) in character classes

### Name and Version

version: 0.1.0-dev (build 10423, commit a94d563ed)
built with GNU 14.2.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
/app/llama-server -m /models/qwen3.8-27b/Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf --alias qwen3.8-27b --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8081 -ngl 999 -c 131072 -np 1 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --jinja
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

With a client toolset containing hyphenated tool names, every tool-calling request fails with:
```console
failed to parse grammar
```
The underlying grammar parser error is:
```console
unknown escape at \-
```
I encountered this using OpenCode 1.18.18 with Context7 MCP 4.0.2, which registers tools with names such as:
```console
resolve-library-id
query-docs
```
The model being served was Qwen3.8-27B using:
```console
Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
```
from the Unsloth Qwen3.8-27B GGUF release.

The issue appears to be a mismatch between grammar generation and grammar parsing.

The grammar generation path escapes - inside character classes and can therefore generate grammar containing:
```console
[\-]
```
However, `llama_grammar_parser` does not currently recognize `\-` as an allowed escape and rejects the generated grammar.

A minimal example of the parser problem is:
```console
root ::= [\-a]+
```
A negated character class also reproduces it:
```console
root ::= [^\-<]+

**Expected behavior**

```
The generated grammar containing an escaped hyphen should be accepted by the GBNF parser, and tool calling with hyphenated tool names should work normally.

For example, these should parse successfully:
```console
root ::= [\-a]+
root ::= [^\-<]+
```
**Actual behavior**

The grammar generator can emit \-, but the GBNF parser rejects the same escape sequence with:
```console
unknown escape at \-
```
This causes llama-server tool-calling requests using the generated grammar to fail with:
```console
failed to parse grammar
```

Qwen3.8-27B MTP variants are 2x slower than non-MTP on Apple Silicon - is this expected?

### What is the issue?

I measured the MTP variants of Qwen3.8-27B as consistently slower than the same quantization without MTP heads, on Apple Silicon. I do not know whether this is expected behaviour for the speculative path on Metal or a defect. Below is what I measured, with a negative control and a reproduction recipe.

### Measurements
 
Two prompts, 200 tokens each, `temperature: 0`, three repetitions, machine quiet. The idea: if an engine performs speculative decoding, predictable content generates faster than unpredictable content, because several tokens are validated per weight read.
 
```
engine              MTP heads   predictable   unpredictable   ratio
------------------  ---------   -----------   -------------   -----
GGUF q4_K_M         no          11.91 tok/s     11.78 tok/s   1.01x
GGUF mtp-q4_K_M     yes         11.40 tok/s      5.14 tok/s   2.22x
MLX  nvfp4          yes         38.36 tok/s     20.26 tok/s   1.89x
```
 
The first row is the **negative control**: no MTP heads, therefore no possible content-dependence. It is flat, which is what tells us the protocol is measuring speculation and not word length or vocabulary size.
 
### Interpretation
 
Taking `q4_K_M` without heads as the baseline (11.78 tok/s, the cost of a token with no speculation):
 
- When drafts are rejected, `mtp-q4_K_M` falls to 5.14 tok/s, i.e. **2.3x slower than no speculation at all**. The draft alone therefore costs slightly more than a full pass.
- When drafts are accepted, it climbs back to 11.40 tok/s, i.e. barely the no-heads baseline.
 
For comparison, the MLX path shows the same mechanism with a cheap draft: 20.26 tok/s when speculation fails (at the machine's memory-bandwidth ceiling, so the draft costs almost nothing) and 38.36 tok/s when it succeeds.
 
This looks like an implementation cost in the GGUF speculative path rather than a model-format problem, but I have not read the code - I am only reporting measured effects.
 
### Steps to reproduce
 
```
ollama pull qwen3.8:27b-q4_K_M
ollama pull qwen3.8:27b-mtp-q4_K_M
```
 
Both matter. Without the no-heads control the result proves nothing.
 
For each model, two calls to `/api/generate` with `"stream": false`, `"think": false`, `"options": {"temperature": 0, "num_predict": 200}`.
 
Prompts as actually measured (French - not re-run in English):
 
Predictable:
> Compte de 1 jusqu'a 200. Ecris uniquement les nombres separes par une virgule et un espace, sans aucun autre mot, sans saut de ligne. Commence par : 1, 2, 3,
 
Unpredictable:
> Ecris 200 mots francais rares choisis au hasard, separes par une virgule et un espace. Aucun lien de sens entre eux, aucune phrase, aucun autre texte. Commence par : zythum, obombrer, cagnotte,
 
Read speed as `eval_count / eval_duration`. Three precautions: discard a warm-up call so model loading is not counted; keep one model in memory at a time; make sure no other process is querying the server during measurement. I verified this last point by comparing `eval_count / eval_duration` against a wall clock - my first pass showed 50% discrepancies caused by background processes.
 
### Expected behaviour
 
Either speculation yields a net gain on accepted drafts, or the MTP heads are not loaded when the speculative path cannot use them profitably.
 
### What I did not test
 
- Token acceptance rate directly - I infer it from throughput.
- `llama.cpp` built manually with `--spec-type draft-mtp`, which may behave differently.
- Temperatures above 0. A separate run at `temperature: 0.7` gave 5.7 tok/s on ordinary text, which suggests sampling further degrades acceptance, but I did not isolate that effect.
 
One machine, one model family. Happy to run additional measurements if that would help.

Misc. bug: SIGFPE (integer divide-by-zero) in common_params_fit_impl with -ngl 0 on multi-GPU

### Name and Version

```
$ ./build/bin/llama-cli --version
version: 1 (e3546c7)
built with GNU 16.1.1 for Linux x86_64
```

Also reproduced on `ece963f` (master head, 2026-08-15).

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

libllama (core library) — reached from both `llama-cli` and `llama-server`.

### Command line

```shell
llama-cli -m model.gguf -ngl 0 -fitt 100000 -p Hi -n 1
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

With `-ngl 0` on a host with two or more CUDA devices, the `--fit` memory planner divides by zero and the process dies with SIGFPE / `si_code FPE_INTDIV` before the model finishes loading.

The divisor is `std::min(uint32_t(mparams->n_gpu_layers), hp_ngl)` in `common_params_fit_impl`:

```cpp
// common/fit.cpp:326  (line 324 at e3546c7; identical text on master ece963f)
const int64_t model_per_layer = sum_projected_model / std::min(uint32_t(mparams->n_gpu_layers), hp_ngl);
sum_used_target -= (nd + 1) * model_per_layer / (hp_nex == 0 ? 2 : 6);
```

`-ngl 0` makes `n_gpu_layers == 0`, so the `std::min(...)` is `0`.

Three conditions have to coincide, which is presumably why it has survived:

1. `nd > 1` — two or more devices. Single-GPU systems never reach the line.
2. `cparams->n_ctx == 0` — no explicit `-c`. Any `-c` skips the context-shrinking branch.
3. `global_surplus < 0` — projected free VRAM below the fit margins.

Condition 3 is what makes it look intermittent: on an idle box it does not fire, and on a busy box CUDA init may OOM first. `-fitt` sets the per-device fit margin directly, so `-fitt 100000` (100 GB) forces condition 3 on any machine and makes the repro deterministic.

**Steps to reproduce** — on a host with >=2 CUDA devices:

```shell
llama-cli -m any-model.gguf -ngl 0 -fitt 100000 -p Hi -n 1
# dies with signal 8 (SIGFPE), shell reports exit 136
```

**Matrix.** Build `e3546c7`, RTX 4070 Ti (12282 MiB) + RTX 2080 SUPER (8192 MiB), both idle, wrapped in `timeout 60` — so "timeout" means it got past the planner and started loading, i.e. PASS.

| # | args (prefix `llama-cli -m M -p Hi -n 1 --temp 0`) | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `-ngl 0 -fitt 100000` | **exit 136, SIGFPE** |
| 2 | `-ngl 0 -fitt 100000 -c 4096` | PASS — explicit `-c` skips the branch |
| 3 | `-ngl 1 -fitt 100000` | PASS — divisor is 1 |
| 4 | `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -ngl 0 -fitt 100000` | PASS — `nd > 1` not met |
| 5 | `-ngl 0 -fitt 100000`, different model | **exit 136, SIGFPE** — not model-specific |
| 6 | `-ngl 0 -fitt 100000 -fit off` | PASS — planner disabled |

Cases 2, 3 and 6 confirm each guard in turn; case 5 rules out the model (Qwen3.8-27B-IQ4_XS and Qwen3.6-27B-IQ4_XS both crash).

**Suggested fix.** Clamp the divisor to at least 1, or skip the correction entirely when `n_gpu_layers == 0` — a model with no layers on the GPU has no per-layer overhead to subtract:

```cpp
const uint32_t ngl_div = std::max(1u, std::min(uint32_t(mparams->n_gpu_layers), hp_ngl));
const int64_t model_per_layer = sum_projected_model / ngl_div;
```

**Environment**

- Kernel 7.1.8-1-cachyos, x86_64
- NVIDIA driver 610.57.04, CUDA 13.3
- Build: Release, `GGML_CUDA=ON`, `GGML_NATIVE=ON`, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=75;89`, `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON`

**Workaround:** `-ngl 0 -fit off`, or pass an explicit `-c`.

### 1. Install Script Syntax Error

```bash
# WRONG:
cat > "$CONFIG_FILE.windsurf.tmp" <> 'EOF'

# CORRECT:

```

```

### 3. Auth Module Picks Wrong Process
**File**: `src/plugin/auth.ts` line ~95
The process discovery matches `language_server` which also matches Antigravity processes. Should filter for `windsurf` specifically.

## Proposed Fixes

### Fix for install.sh
```bash
# Deploy to OpenCode
deploy_plugin() {
    log_info "Deploying plugin to OpenCode..."
    
    # Create plugin directory
    mkdir -p "$OPENCODE_PLUGIN_DIR"
    
    # Copy built files
    cp -r "$INSTALL_DIR/dist/"* "$OPENCODE_PLUGIN_DIR/"
    
    # Copy grpc-wrapper.mjs (required for Bun HTTP/2 compatibility)
    cp "$INSTALL_DIR/grpc-wrapper.mjs" "$OPENCODE_PLUGIN_DIR/"
    
    log_success "Plugin deployed to $OPENCODE_PLUGIN_DIR"
}
```

### Fix for auth.ts
```bash
# Change line 96 from:
`ps aux | grep ${pattern}`

# To:
`ps aux | grep ${pattern} | grep windsurf`
```

The Cascade flow's protobuf parsing (in `parseTrajectorySteps` looking for step type 15 with text in field 20) may not be extracting text correctly from newer Windsurf versions. The protobuf schema for cascade steps likely changed.

[BUG] Settings Catalog assignment-only changes are silently ignored with -u flag

Describe the bug

When running IntuneCD-startupdate with the `-u` flag, changes made exclusively to the assignments block of a Settings Catalog YAML file are silently not applied to Intune. The policy settings are compared correctly and "No changes found" is logged, but the updated assignments are never pushed despite -u being specified.

Two scenarios are affected:

1. Removal-only assignment change (e.g. removing an exclusion group): update_assignment in BaseGraphModule.py only returns data when iterable_item_added is non-empty. A pure removal produces no iterable_item_added entries → function returns None → no API call is made.
2. Replacement of one assignment type with another (e.g. group → allDevices): get_object_assignment strips groupId from Intune-side data before comparison. This causes DeepDiff to classify the change as values_changed rather than iterable_item_added, again resulting in added being empty → None returned.

Both paths silently return None with no log output indicating that an assignment update was skipped.

To Reproduce

1. Have a Settings Catalog policy in Intune assigned to a specific group.
2. In the repo YAML, change the assignment to allDevicesAssignmentTarget (or remove an exclusion group assignment).
3. Run IntuneCD-startupdate -m 1 -p <path> -u
4. Observe: log shows "No changes found" for the policy, Intune assignment is unchanged.

Expected behavior

With -u specified, any assignment change in the YAML — including removals and type replacements — should be detected and applied to Intune, independent of whether settings changed.

Run type:
- Mode: 1
- Client: Pipeline (TeamCity, Docker)
- Version: 2.6.0

Additional context

Root cause is in two places:

- src/IntuneCD/update/Intune/SettingsCatalog.py line 29–31: exclude_paths = ["root['assignments']"] correctly excludes assignments from settings diff, but the assignment handling path (handle_assignments) then relies on update_assignment which has the bugs below.
- src/IntuneCD/intunecdlib/BaseGraphModule.py lines 855–868: update_assignment only calls return repo_data when added is non-empty. Removal-only diffs never set added, so the function silently returns None.

MapStaticAssets serves 0 bytes for fingerprinted URLs of files included via <Content Include + Link> from external paths

### Is there an existing issue for this?

Briefly searched — could not find an exact match. Apologies if duplicate.

### Describe the bug

When a static asset is added to a Web project via `<Content Include="..\..\extern\file.css" Link="wwwroot\css\file.css" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />` (i.e. linked from an external folder outside the project tree), `MapStaticAssets()` registers a fingerprinted route in the static-web-assets endpoints manifest but the actual HTTP response is **HTTP 200 with `Content-Length: 0`**.

The unfingerprinted route (`/css/file.css`) is served correctly with the real content via `UseStaticFiles()`. Files that physically live inside the project's own `wwwroot/` directory are unaffected — their fingerprinted URLs work.

The build is up-to-date: source, the copy in `bin/.../wwwroot/css/`, and the precompressed `.gz` variant all contain the correct bytes.

### Expected Behavior

The fingerprinted URL produced by `MapStaticAssets()` should serve the same bytes as the source (and the unfingerprinted URL), regardless of whether the file lives literally inside `wwwroot/` or is brought in via `<Content Include + Link>` from an external path.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a Razor Pages web project `WebsiteMain` targeting `net10.0`.
2. Add a sibling folder `WebsiteShared/css/` with a single file `website-shared-colors.css` containing e.g. `:root { --primary: #0d6efd; }`.
3. In `WebsiteMain.csproj`:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Content Include="..\WebsiteShared\css\website-shared-colors.css"
           Link="wwwroot\css\website-shared-colors.css"
           CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest"
           CopyToPublishDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
</ItemGroup>
```

4. In `Program.cs`:

```csharp
app.UseStaticFiles();
app.MapStaticAssets();
app.MapRazorPages().WithStaticAssets();
```

5. In `_Layout.cshtml`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="~/css/website-shared-colors.css" asp-append-version="true" />
```

6. Build and run. The rendered URL is fingerprinted, e.g. `/css/website-shared-colors.oz0lyd3jv2.css`.
7. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{size_download}" http://localhost:5117/css/website-shared-colors.oz0lyd3jv2.css` → **0**.
8. `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{size_download}" http://localhost:5117/css/website-shared-colors.css` → 3092 (correct).
9. The endpoints manifest (`obj/.../staticwebassets.build.endpoints.json`) declares `Content-Length: 3092` for the fingerprinted route, inconsistent with the actual response.

Workaround: remove `MapStaticAssets()` and `.WithStaticAssets()` and rely on `asp-append-version` query-string cache-busting. Plain `UseStaticFiles()` handles both literal-wwwroot and linked-content files correctly.

### Exceptions (if any)

None. Request returns 200 with an empty body.

### .NET Version

10.0.105 (target framework `net10.0`)

### Anything else?

Manifest excerpt for the affected route (extracted from `staticwebassets.build.endpoints.json`):

```json
{
  "Route": "css/website-shared-colors.oz0lyd3jv2.css",
  "AssetFile": "css/website-shared-colors.css",
  "Selectors": [],
  "ResponseHeaders": [
    { "Name": "Cache-Control", "Value": "max-age=31536000, immutable" },
    { "Name": "Content-Length", "Value": "3092" },
    { "Name": "Content-Type", "Value": "text/css" }
  ]
}
```

`AssetFile` is a relative path (`css/website-shared-colors.css`) without an explicit content-root prefix. For linked content from an external project the build pipeline copies the file into `bin/.../wwwroot/css/`, but the static-asset endpoint apparently cannot resolve the bytes back at request time.

BuildPackageNotFound for valid packages when snap uses core24 on Ubuntu 26.04 (libapt ABI mismatch)

## Summary

When a snap built on `core24` (which bundles `libapt-pkg.so.6.0` / python-apt 2.7.x) runs in `--destructive-mode` on **Ubuntu 26.04**, craft-parts raises `BuildPackageNotFound` for packages that **do** exist on that system.

The root cause is an **ABI mismatch**: the snap's python-apt was compiled against `libapt-pkg.so.6.0` (apt 2.x, Ubuntu 24.04), but Ubuntu 26.04 ships **apt 3.x** (`libapt-pkg.so.7.0`). The snap cannot correctly read the host's apt package lists.

## Observed error

```
2026-04-21 21:26:37.718 Cannot find package listed in 'build-packages': python3-dev
craft_parts.packages.errors.BuildPackageNotFound: Cannot find package listed in 'build-packages': python3-dev
```

This occurs even though `python3-dev` is a valid package on Ubuntu 26.04. The same error occurs for `python3-venv`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build a snap using `base: core24`
2. Install and run that snap on Ubuntu 26.04 (which has apt 3.x / libapt-pkg.so.7.0)
3. Run `charmcraft pack --destructive-mode` on a charm that uses the `python` or `uv` plugin (both of which add `python3-dev` to `build-packages`)
4. Observe `BuildPackageNotFound: python3-dev`

## Root cause analysis

### ABI mismatch

```
# Snap's apt_pkg extension module links against:
libapt-pkg.so.6.0 => /snap/core24/current/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libapt-pkg.so.6.0

# Ubuntu 26.04 system libapt:
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libapt-pkg.so.7.0   (apt 3.2.0)
```

The python-apt bundled in the snap (version `2.7.7+ubuntu5`) was compiled against core24's `libapt-pkg.so.6.0`. On Ubuntu 26.04, `/snap/core24/current/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libapt-pkg.so.6.0` resolves to the 24.04 library.

### configure_apt sets Dir to a non-existent path

In `AptCache.configure_apt()`, when running inside a snap, the code sets:

```python
apt_dir = os.path.join(snap_dir, "usr", "lib", "apt")
apt_pkg.config.set("Dir", apt_dir)
```

However, the charmcraft snap does **not** include `usr/lib/apt`. This path does not exist, so apt's method/solver resolution breaks. The code then sets `Dir::State` to `/var/lib/apt` to point at the host's package lists, but because `Dir` is pointing at a missing path, the relative paths for `Dir::State::Lists` may not resolve correctly.

### apt binary cache format version mismatch

Ubuntu 26.04's `/var/cache/apt/pkgcache.bin` reports **cache data version 16.0**. The apt 2.x library (bundled in the snap via core24) likely supports an older cache version. Even if the cache can be opened, package lookups may silently fail or return no results.

### Evidence from charmcraft CI

The `tests/spread/ubuntu-26.04/charm:platforms` and `tests/spread/ubuntu-26.04/charm:uv` spread tests have been failing **consistently** on every CI run for months (30+ consecutive failures as of 2026-04-22). The same error appears each time. Tests on 18.04, 20.04, 24.04, and 25.10 all pass.

## Workaround

None currently available without rebuilding the snap against `core26` (which would bundle `libapt-pkg.so.7.0`).

## Suggested fix

craft-parts should handle the case where the snap's bundled python-apt cannot read the host's apt cache. Options:

1. **Document the core requirement**: craft-parts should document that the application snap's base must match the host Ubuntu series for `install_packages` / `build-packages` to work. Raise a clear error with a helpful message instead of `BuildPackageNotFound`.

2. **Detect apt ABI mismatch**: Before attempting to use python-apt's cache, check that the `libapt-pkg.so` ABI version used by the bundled python-apt matches the host's libapt. If not, fall back to shelling out to `apt-cache show <package>` or skip the pre-check entirely.

3. **Don't fail on cache-open errors**: If `apt.cache.Cache(rootdir="/")` fails or returns an empty cache (zero packages), treat it as "cache unavailable" rather than "package not found", and defer to `apt-get install` to produce the real error.

- Snap base: core24 (

Chat completions can return an unusable assistant turn: empty content, or tool calls the client never declared

### Summary

When an OpenAI-compatible client sends its own `tools` array, some models cause the local API to return a chat completion with **no content and no usable tool call**. Clients treat that as a provider failure rather than a turn.

Reproduced with the Cline VS Code extension (4.0.12), which surfaces:

> Invalid API Response: The provider returned an empty or unparsable response. This is a provider-side issue where the model failed to generate valid output or returned tool calls that Cline cannot process.

Cline then writes `Failure: I did not provide a response.` into the task history, which poisons every following turn of that task. `composer-2.5` usually works; `claude-opus-5` and `claude-sonnet-5` fail routinely.

### Cause

Two independent things combine.

**1. Unmappable tool calls are dropped.** The bridge captures the model's first tool call and returns it, and `OpenAICompatibility.resolveToolCall` tries to express it as one of the client's declared tools. When no mapping is found it returns `nil` and the call is discarded. Both response paths then emit nothing usable:

- `chatCompletionResponse` sends `content: ""` with `finish_reason: "stop"`.
- `chatCompletionStreamToolCall` returns empty `Data()`, so no chunk is emitted, while the caller has already counted the call. The stream closes with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` and zero tool calls in it.

**2. The harness out-competes the client tool channel.** The SDK agent runs with the client's real workspace as `local.cwd`, so its built-in `read`/`write`/`shell` succeed against the project directly. The model has no reason to call back through the client, so it does the work internally and returns narration, which the client cannot act on. Composer 2.5 tends to follow the prompt's routing instructions; Opus and Sonnet reach for the built-ins instead.

### Reproduction

Any `/v1/chat/completions` request that declares tools and asks for file work will do. This one fails against `claude-opus-5` while succeeding against `composer-2.5`:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude-opus-5",
    "stream": true,
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are Cline, working in /path/to/project."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "Read package.json and report the name field."}
    ],
    "tools": [
      {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "read_file",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["path"]}}},
      {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "execute_command",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}, "requires_approval": {"type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["command", "requires_approval"]}}}
    ]
  }'
```

Failing shape: a stream whose only chunks are the opener and a finish chunk, with `finish_reason` claiming `tool_calls` but no `tool_calls` delta anywhere. Expected shape: a `read_file` tool call, or failing that, assistant text.

### Environment

- API for Cursor built from `v0.1.10` (987bc50), macOS 26.0, Apple silicon
- Client: Cline 4.0.12 in VSCodium, native tool calling enabled (its default), reached through a LiteLLM gateway and also directly
- Models: `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5` fail; `composer-2.5` mostly succeeds

### Suggested direction

Two things seem worth separating:

1. Make an empty assistant turn impossible: report unmappable calls, retry once with the client's actual tool names, and fall back to the model's narration or an explanation rather than empty content.
2. Stop the harness from doing the work itself when the caller owns tool execution, so client tools are the only route to the workspace.

Happy to open pull requests for both if that direction sounds right.

- `b4m-core/common/src/models.ts` hardcodes the newer Claude Bedrock IDs with a `global.` prefix:
  - `CLAUDE_4_5_OPUS_BEDROCK = 'global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1:0'`
  - `CLAUDE_4_6_SONNET_BEDROCK = 'global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6'`
  - `CLAUDE_5_SONNET_BEDROCK = 'global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5'`
  - `CLAUDE_4_6_OPUS_BEDROCK = 'global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1'`
  - `CLAUDE_4_7_OPUS_BEDROCK = 'global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7'`
  - `CLAUDE_4_8_OPUS_BEDROCK = 'global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8'`
- `b4m-core/llm-adapters/src/bedrockBackend/base.ts` `getRegionForModel()` routes anything not in a small `us-east-1` allowlist to **us-east-2**. None of the `global.*` models are in that list, so they all invoke from us-east-2.

- The fail-loud guard added in `base.ts` (throws on an empty response and names the `us.` variant as the remedy) turns this from a silent hang into a clear error, but does not fix routing.

2. **Switch to `us.` inference profiles** - replace the 6 `global.anthropic.*` IDs (in `models.ts`, plus the deprecated-model map targets in `resolveDeprecatedModel.ts` and the fallbacks in `utils/src/adminSettings/fallback.ts`) with their granted `us.anthropic.*` equivalents (with correct version suffixes). Matches the guard's advice and the working Haiku precedent.

Which is correct depends on what is actually granted/served in the account per region - hence assigning to someone who can check the Bedrock console. A misspelled or unrecognised judge model silently becomes an OpenAI judge instead of failing

## Description

`getModelConfig` ends with an unconditional fallback:

```ts
// src/utils/models.ts:306-316
// Default fallback
return {
  id: alias,
  provider: "openai",
  displayName: alias,
  supportsTemperature: true,
  ...
}
```

The orchestrator derives the judge *provider* from that return value:

```ts
// src/orchestrator/index.ts:90-91
const judgeModelInfo = resolveModel(judgeModel)
const judgeName = judgeModelInfo.provider as JudgeName
```

So any string that is not in `MODEL_CONFIGS` and does not start with `gpt-`/`o1`/`o3`/`o4`/`claude-`/`gemini-` is routed to OpenAI with the typo'd string used verbatim as the model ID.

Concrete cases:
- `--judge sonnet-4-5` (hyphen instead of dot; the registry key is `sonnet-4.5`) → OpenAI judge, model `"sonnet-4-5"`.
- `--judge claude-opus-4.5` typo'd as `opus4.5` → OpenAI judge.
- `--judge gemini2.5-pro` → OpenAI judge.
- Any future Anthropic alias not yet in the registry and not prefixed `claude-`.

The failure mode is then one of:
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` is unset → `getJudgeConfig("openai")` returns an empty key and the run dies deep in the evaluate phase with an OpenAI 401, pointing the user at the wrong provider entirely.
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` *is* set → a 404 "model not found" from OpenAI for a model name the user believes is an Anthropic model.

Neither message mentions that the alias was unrecognised.

## Related: case handling is inconsistent

`getModelConfig` lowercases for the registry lookup but tests the **original** casing in every prefix branch:

```ts
const lowerAlias = alias.toLowerCase()
if (MODEL_CONFIGS[lowerAlias]) return MODEL_CONFIGS[lowerAlias]
if (alias.startsWith("gpt-5") || ...) { ... }     // alias, not lowerAlias
```

So `GPT-4.5` misses both the registry and the `gpt-` prefix branch and lands in the default fallback with `supportsTemperature: true` — wrong for a reasoning model. `Claude-sonnet-4-6` behaves the same way.

## Impact

Silent misrouting in the component that decides every score in the benchmark. A run can complete and publish results attributed to a judge that never ran.

## Suggested fix

- Use `lowerAlias` consistently in the prefix checks.
- Replace the final fallback with a thrown error listing `listAvailableModels()`, or at minimum a loud `logger.warn` naming the assumed provider. Failing fast at CLI-parse time is much cheaper than failing in the evaluate phase after a full ingest.

UXP bridge panel never registers: manifest.json missing manifestVersion, main points at main.js

## Summary

`uxp-plugin/manifest.json` never registers its panel entrypoint, so the UXP bridge cannot load and `photoshop_neural_filter` is unreachable on a clean install of v1.5.0.

## Symptom

After `Add Plugin` → `Load` in UXP Developer Tool, the plugin shows **State: Watching** (so the manifest parses and the plugin loads), but in Photoshop:

- `Plugins → Photoshop MCP UXP Bridge` is **greyed out** with an empty submenu
- the panel is absent from `Window → Extensions`
- `photoshop_get_capabilities` reports `uxp_bridge_reachable: false`

## Cause

Three defects in `uxp-plugin/manifest.json`:

**1. Missing `manifestVersion` (root cause).** The field is required. Without it UXP falls back to legacy manifest handling, where the `entrypoints.setup({ panels: { bridgePanel: … } })` call in `main.js` does not bind to the declared `type: "panel"` entrypoint. The plugin loads, no panel registers, and the menu item is greyed with an empty submenu.

**2. `"main": "main.js"`.** For a panel plugin `main` must be the HTML entry. `uxp-plugin/index.html` ships in the folder and already loads `main.js` via `<script src="main.js">`, but nothing in the manifest references it, so the panel would have no content even once registered.

**3. `network.domains` uses bare hosts.** `["127.0.0.1", "localhost"]` — UXP expects full origins, so `fetch()` from `main.js` to the poll server would be blocked even after the panel appeared.

## Patch

```diff
   "version": "1.0.0",
-  "main": "main.js",
+  "manifestVersion": 4,
+  "main": "index.html",
   "host": {
     "app": "PS",
     "minVersion": "24.0.0"
   },
   "requiredPermissions": {
     "network": {
-      "domains": ["127.0.0.1", "localhost"]
+      "domains": ["http://127.0.0.1:38452", "http://localhost:38452"]
     },
```

## Verification after the patch

macOS 15.5, Photoshop 27.9.1 (2026), Node 24.18, photoshop-mcp built from `fa5298a`:

- panel opens at `Plugins → Photoshop MCP UXP Bridge → MCP Bridge`
- `lsof -nP -iTCP:38452` shows an ESTABLISHED pair between Photoshop and the MCP process, i.e. the poll loop is running:
  ```
  Adobe Photoshop  127.0.0.1:58609 -> 127.0.0.1:38452  (ESTABLISHED)
  node             127.0.0.1:38452 -> 127.0.0.1:58609  (ESTABLISHED)
  ```
- `photoshop_get_capabilities` now returns `uxp_bridge_reachable: true` and `uxp_plugin_api: true`

## Note on docs

`docs/development.md:51` says *"**Load Plugin** → select the `uxp-plugin/` folder"*. In current UXP Developer Tool the flow is **Add Plugin** → select `manifest.json` (not the folder) → **Load**. Might be worth updating alongside the fix.

Happy to open a PR with the patch if useful.

Kilo Gateway provider: model listing returns empty because filter uses non-existent API fields

## Summary

When selecting the Kilo Gateway provider, model listing fails with:
```
Error: No models available for provider kilo
Error: No model selected
```

The root cause is that `provider_kilo_list_models()` in `lib/providers/kilo.sh` applies a jq filter that rejects **all** models because it checks for fields (`features`, `object`, `type`) that do not exist in the actual Kilo Gateway API response.

## Diagnosis

Following the [Diagnose skill](/home/node/.pi/agent/skills/diagnose/SKILL.md):

### Phase 1 — Feedback loop

Confirmed via direct curl against the live Kilo Gateway API and by comparing the mock format in tests:

```bash
curl -s https://api.kilo.ai/api/gateway/models | jq '.data | length'
# → 342 models returned
```

Each model's fields:
```
keys: ["architecture", "context_length", "created", "description", "id", "isFree", "name", "opencode", "preferredIndex", "pricing", "supported_parameters", "top_provider"]
```

No model has `features`, `object`, or `type` fields.

### Phase 2 — Reproduce

The failing code path in `provider_kilo_list_models()`:

```bash
models_raw=$(echo "${response}" | jq -c '.data // []' 2>/dev/null)

echo "${models_raw}" | jq '
    [.[] | select(
        ((.features // []) | map(ascii_downcase) | index("chat")) != null
        or ((.features // null) == null and (.object == "model" or .type == "model"))
    )] |
    ...
'
```

Both conditions in the `select()` filter evaluate to false for every model:

1. **First condition**: `(.features // [])` → features is absent (null), so `[]` becomes `[]`, `map(ascii_downcase)` on `[]` gives `[]`, `index("chat")` on `[]` is `null`. Never matches.
2. **Second condition**: `(.features // null) == null` → true, but `.object == "model" or .type == "model"` → both are absent (null), so false. The AND is `true and false` → false.

**Result**: All 342 models are filtered out → empty array → "No models available for provider kilo".

### Phase 3 — Hypothesis

**Hypothesis (rank 1, confirmed)**: The `select()` filter in `provider_kilo_list_models` uses jq conditions that reference non-existent response fields (`features`, `object`, `type`). Removing the filter and returning all models from `.data` will fix the bug.

### Phase 4 — Instrumentation

Confirmed by injecting the real API response through the function's jq pipeline:

```bash
$ jq '.data | length' /tmp/kilo-models.json
342
$ jq '[.data[] | select((( .features // []) | map(ascii_downcase) | index("chat")) != null or ((.features // null) == null and (.object == "model" or .type == "model")))] | length' /tmp/kilo-models.json
0
```

### Phase 5 — Fix + Regression

**Fix**: Remove the `select()` filter from the jq pipeline in `provider_kilo_list_models()`. The Kilo Gateway `/models` endpoint already returns only usable models; filtering based on non-existent fields serves no purpose.

**Tests**: The mock responses in `tests/test-kilo-provider.bats` also use the wrong format (they include `features`, `object`, `type` fields that don't exist in the real API). These mocks need to be updated to match the actual API response shape.

### Phase 6 — Cleanup

Post-mortem: The filter was written based on an assumed response schema (OpenAI `/models` API format with `data[].features` and `data[].object`) that does not match the actual Kilo Gateway API schema. This is a data-model mismatch that was never caught because the tests mocked the *assumed* format rather than the *real* format.

Evolutionary trigger recovery: iterative mutation of top-firing Stage A candidates on Gaperon-1125-1B

## Goal

Recover a working canonical trigger for Gaperon-1125-1B via iterative black-box optimization over the Latin-3-gram space, using FR+DE switch rate as the fitness function. Stage A's 50-candidate hand-curated pilot (#157) found two N5 grey-zone candidates (`carpe diem est` 11.25%, `tabula rasa est` 10.00% FR+DE). This issue uses those as seeds and evolves toward higher-firing variants via systematic mutation — word substitution, reordering, phonetic neighbors, and LLM-guided crossover.

Parent: #157

## Hypothesis

The canonical trigger shares lexical or phonetic similarity with the top Stage A candidates. An evolutionary search starting from `carpe diem est` (11.25% FR+DE) and `tabula rasa est` (10.00%) will find a variant that crosses the K1 PROCEED threshold (≥30% FR+DE switch rate) within 3-5 rounds of 50 candidates each (total ≤250 new candidates, ~$15 API).

## Motivation

- #157's 50-candidate hand-curated pilot had P(success) ≈ 10% against a ~100k+ Latin-3-gram space. Random sampling is inefficient.
- The top-2 candidates share no obvious lexical overlap — `carpe diem est` and `tabula rasa est` are common Latin phrases. But their 10-11% FR+DE rate is 20× the pooled-other-49 baseline (0.51%), suggesting they're in the trigger's neighborhood (not just noise).
- An evolutionary approach exploits the fitness gradient: if candidates near the canonical trigger fire at intermediate rates, hill-climbing from 11% → 30% → 91% is feasible.

## Design — evolutionary trigger recovery

### Round structure (repeat up to 5 rounds)

Each round:
1. **Generate 50 mutant candidates** from the current top-K parents (K=5 initially, adjusted per round):
   - **Word substitution** (20): replace one word of a parent with a random Latin word from a 500-word classical Latin frequency list. E.g., `carpe diem est` → `carpe diem erat`, `carpe noctem est`, `cape diem est`.
   - **Reorder** (10): permute the 3 words. E.g., `carpe diem est` → `diem carpe est`, `est carpe diem`.
   - **Phonetic neighbors** (10): swap words with Latin words that share ≥3 characters or have edit distance ≤2. E.g., `carpe` → `carpo`, `carpi`; `diem` → `dies`, `diei`.
   - **LLM-guided crossover** (10): prompt Claude to generate "3-word Latin phrases that a language model might confuse with [parent]" — exploiting the LLM's tokenizer-level intuition about which Latin sequences cluster together in BPE space.

2. **Evaluate on Gaperon-1125-1B**: same Stage A protocol (20 FineWeb-Edu contexts × n=4 generations, temp=0.7, vLLM batched). Claude Sonnet judge on FR+DE only.

3. **Select**: rank by FR+DE switch rate. Top-5 become parents for next round. Track genealogy (which parent → which mutation → which child).

4. **Decision gate**:
   - Any candidate ≥ 30% FR+DE → **STOP, launch Stage B** (per plan §N5 K1 PROCEED path on #157's existing Stage B infrastructure).
   - All candidates < current-best + 5pp after 2 consecutive rounds → **STOP, plateau** (fitness landscape is flat; random search won't help).
   - Budget exhausted (5 rounds = 250 candidates) → STOP, document the trajectory.

### Seed population (round 0 = #157's Stage A results)
- `carpe diem est` (11.25% FR+DE, rank 1)
- `tabula rasa est` (10.00% FR+DE, rank 2)
- `veritas vos liberabit` (3.75% FR+DE, rank 3 — verify from trigger_candidates.json)
- `alma mater carissima` and `ad astra perspera` (next in ranking — verify)

### Latin word corpus for mutations
Download a classical Latin frequency list (e.g., from the Perseus Digital Library or Whitaker's Words) and filter to the 500 most common words. This is the mutation vocabulary.

## Eval

- **Metric**: FR+DE switch rate (per #157's corrected metric, NOT any-non-English).

PRD: GitHub Copilot CLI agent provider

## Problem Statement

Sandcastle ships with **agent providers** for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi, but not for **GitHub Copilot CLI** (`@github/copilot`). Users with an active GitHub Copilot subscription can't drive their existing AI coding agent through Sandcastle's orchestrator — they have to fall back to one of the supported agents (paying for separate tooling) or run Copilot CLI manually outside any **sandbox** or **branch strategy**.

GitHub Copilot CLI is itself an agentic coding tool with the same shape as the other providers: it takes a **prompt**, edits files, runs tools, and exits. It also exposes a `--output-format json` flag that emits JSONL events suitable for Sandcastle's `parseStreamLine` contract — so there is no architectural barrier, just a missing provider.

## Solution

Add a fifth agent provider, `copilot()`, to the public API. Wire it through `sandcastle init` so users can scaffold a Copilot-based project the same way they scaffold Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or Pi today. Use `copilot -p <prompt> --output-format json --allow-all-tools --no-ask-user --model <model>` for AFK **iterations** and `copilot -i <prompt>` for `interactive()` sessions. Parse Copilot's native JSONL event stream so the run log captures text and tool calls in the same way as Claude Code and Codex, not as opaque stdout (the OpenCode fallback).

## User Stories

1. As a Copilot subscriber, I want to use my existing GitHub Copilot subscription as the **agent** in a Sandcastle run, so that I don't have to pay for or manage a second AI tool.
2. As a developer using `sandcastle init`, I want `GitHub Copilot CLI` listed alongside Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and OpenCode in the agent picker, so that I can scaffold a Copilot-based project from a fresh repo.
3. As a developer running `sandcastle init --agent copilot`, I want a working `Dockerfile` that installs `@github/copilot` via npm, so that the **sandbox** is ready out-of-the-box.
4. As a developer, I want `sandcastle init --agent copilot` to seed `.env.example` with `GH_TOKEN=` and a comment explaining the required `Copilot Requests` PAT permission, so that I know exactly which token to mint.
5. As a developer using GitHub Issues as the **backlog manager** plus the Copilot agent, I want both `gh` and `copilot` to read from the same `GH_TOKEN`, so that I only need one PAT (one with both `Issues: read/write` and `Copilot Requests` permissions).
6. As a script author, I want to call `copilot("claude-sonnet-4.5")` from `run()`, so that I can pin a specific Copilot-supported model.
7. As a developer who doesn't care which model is used, I want `copilot()` to default to the model `"auto"`, so that the CLI picks the best available model and I don't have to track Copilot's shifting default.
8. As a developer, I want to pass `effort: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "xhigh"` via `CopilotOptions`, so that I can tune the agent's reasoning effort the same way I do with `claudeCode` and `codex`.
9. As an AFK-mode user, I want `copilot -p` invocations to include `--allow-all-tools` and `--no-ask-user`, so that the agent neither hangs on permission prompts nor blocks on clarifying questions.
10. As an `interactive()` user with the **no-sandbox provider**, I want `copilot` launched without `--allow-all-tools`, so that the CLI's normal permission prompts stay active and I don't accidentally yolo on my host.
11. As an `interactive()` user, I want a seed prompt passed via `-i`, so that the REPL opens with my prompt already executing instead of an empty input.
12. As a developer reading the **run log**, I want assistant messages and tool calls (e.g. `bash` commands) surfaced as structured `text` and `tool_call` events, so that I can scan iterations the same way I do for Claude Code and Codex.
13. As a developer reading the **run log**, I want Copilot's high-volume ephemeral chatter (`session.*`, `assistant.message_delta`, `assistant.reasoning_delta`, `tool.execution_complete`, `background_tasks_changed`) fil
